ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: object A is placed on a rough inclined plane, and the inclined plane is marked 45°; A is connected through an upward-along-the-inclined-plane spring/light string to a fixed pulley at the upper right, and after the string passes over the pulley it is connected vertically downward to hanging object B. For B, by force balance, the tension in the string T=m_B g. Since sinθ decreases from sin45° to sin30°, f decreases.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are connected with a light string and a spring and pass over a pulley. A is at rest on a rough inclined plane with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$, and B is hanging. It is known that the masses are $\mathrm{m_{A}=3m_{B}}$, and pulley friction is neglected. Now the inclination angle of the inclined plane is decreased from $45^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$, and A is always at rest relative to the inclined plane. How does the static friction force received by object A change?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: The static friction force on object A will decrease
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_standard_answer: The static friction force on object A will decrease
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are connected with a light string and a spring and pass over a pulley. A is at rest on a rough inclined plane with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$, and B is hanging. It is known that the masses are $\mathrm{m_{A}=3m_{B}}$, and pulley friction is neglected. Now the inclination angle of the inclined plane is decreased from $45^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$, and A is always at rest relative to the inclined plane. How does the static friction force received by object A change?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The static friction force on object A will decrease
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: object A is placed on a rough inclined plane, and the inclined plane is marked 45°; A is connected through an upward-along-the-inclined-plane spring/light string to a fixed pulley at the upper right, and after the string passes over the pulley it is connected vertically downward to hanging object B. Therefore the direction of the pulling force of the string or spring on A is upward along the inclined plane, and B is hanging vertically. From the problem statement, m_A=3m_B, the pulley has no friction, the inclination angle of the inclined plane decreases from 45° to 30°, and A is always at rest relative to the inclined plane. For B, by force balance, the tension in the string T=m_B g. For A, analyze along the direction of the inclined plane: the component of A's gravity downward along the inclined plane is m_A g sinθ=3m_B g sinθ. When θ=45°, 3m_B g sin45°>m_B g; when θ=30°, 3m_B g sin30°=1.5m_B g>m_B g, so in both cases A has a tendency to slide downward along the inclined plane, and the direction of the static friction force is upward along the inclined plane in both cases. From static equilibrium, the magnitude of the static friction force is f=3m_B g sinθ-m_B g. Therefore f_45=(3sin45°-1)m_B g, f_30=(3sin30°-1)m_B g. Since sinθ decreases from sin45° to sin30°, f decreases.
